title: Association of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use with risk of gallbladder and biliary diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
authors: He L, Wang J, Ping F, Yang N, Huang J, Li Y, et al.
population: 76 randomised trials of GLP-1 receptor agonists against placebo or other drugs in adults; mean age 57.8 years, 40.5% women; search to June 2021
funder: Supported by grants from the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the Beijing Municipal Natural Science Foundation, the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and the Dongcheng District talent programme. The funders had no role in design, conduct, collection, analysis, interpretation, preparation, review or approval of the manuscript, or the decision to submit.
result: Randomisation to a GLP-1 receptor agonist increased gallbladder or biliary disease (relative risk 1.37, 95% CI 1.23 to 1.52), an absolute excess of 27 (17 to 38) events per 10,000 patients per year; cholelithiasis 1.27 (1.10 to 1.47), cholecystitis 1.36 (1.14 to 1.62), biliary disease 1.55 (1.08 to 2.22). The relative risk was 2.29 (1.64 to 3.18) in 13 weight-loss trials against 1.27 (1.14 to 1.43) in other trials, 1.56 (1.36 to 1.78) at higher against 0.99 (0.73 to 1.33) at lower doses, and 1.40 (1.26 to 1.56) with longer against 0.79 (0.48 to 1.31) with shorter use.
